name: webapp-local
description: Build a working expense splitter - settlement logic, a stdlib HTTP API and a frontend - entirely on LOCAL models: no network, no credential, no token cost. Every harness node is TOOL-LESS, because a 7B given a read tool was measured emitting a hallucinated tool call AS ITS ANSWER; the models only write text and shell nodes do all file I/O. Three deterministic gates heal their own author: split_check runs the settlement against its own reference implementation and hands back a runnable counterexample, api_check drives the real server over HTTP in a child process, and ui_check runs the frontend logic under Node and refuses a page that loads anything from the network. REQUIRES two stanzas in lockstep.toml, `local-fast` and `local-smart` - see flows/demo/README-webapp.md. NOTE the frontend branch depends on `logic-gate` even though it needs nothing from it. That is deliberate and was learned from a run: two healing gates with `rollback: true` whose snapshots overlap in time WILL clobber each other. A rollback's scope is every path changed since ITS baseline (SPEC §9.4.4), not just the paths its own target wrote - so logic-gate's restore discarded the frontend files three times over, and ui-gate then blocked on a module the other branch's rollback had just removed. Serialising the branches is the fix; `heal-target-overlap` does not catch this because the TARGETS are disjoint.

spec.task:
The project is an expense splitter: a group shares costs and the app works out who owes whom.

`backend/split.py` is a PURE module - no I/O, no server, no work at import time - exposing exactly:

    balances(expenses) -> {name: net}
        expenses is a list of {"payer": str, "amount": float, "participants": [str, ...]}
        Each expense splits `amount` EQUALLY among its participants.
        The payer is credited the full amount; each participant is debited amount/len(participants).
        A payer who is also a participant gets both. net > 0 means that person is owed money.

    settle(balances) -> [{"from": str, "to": str, "amount": float}, ...]
        Transfers that bring every balance to zero.
        Match the largest creditor with the largest debtor, move the SMALLER of the two
        magnitudes, and repeat. That gives at most n-1 transfers for n people.
        No self-transfers, and no zero or negative amounts.

Write backend/split.py: exactly those two functions, nothing else.

You have NO TOOLS: no shell, no file access, no search. Everything you need is in this prompt. Output ONLY the file content - no markdown fence, no explanation, no leading or trailing prose.

Write backend/server.py: a Python standard-library HTTP server. No third-party imports.

- It is started as `python backend/server.py <PORT>` and MUST bind that port on 127.0.0.1.
- It imports balances and settle from the split module sitting NEXT TO IT: add the file's own
  directory to sys.path first, then `from split import balances, settle`.
- Keep posted expenses in a module-level list.
- Every response is JSON with Content-Type application/json.

    POST /expenses  body {"payer","amount","participants"}  -> 201 {"ok": true, "count": <total so far>}
    GET  /expenses                                          -> 200 {"expenses": [...]}
    GET  /balances                                          -> 200 {"balances": {name: net}}
    GET  /settlement                                        -> 200 {"settlement": [{"from","to","amount"}]}
    GET  /health                                            -> 200 {"ok": true}
    any other path, GET or POST                             -> 404

Silence the default request logging.

You have NO TOOLS: no shell, no file access, no search. Everything you need is in this prompt. Output ONLY the file content - no markdown fence, no explanation, no leading or trailing prose.

Write frontend/split.js: a pure ES module, no DOM access, exporting exactly:

    formatAmount(n)        -> a string with ALWAYS two decimals: 12.345 -> "12.35", 4 -> "4.00"
    summarise(balances)    -> [{name, text}] one row per person, SORTED BY NAME.
                              text says "<name> is owed <amount>" when they are owed money,
                              "<name> owes <amount>" when they owe, and "<name> is settled"
                              when the balance is within half a cent of zero.
                              Amounts in the text always have two decimals and are positive.
    renderSettlement(list) -> ["ben pays ana 4.00", ...] one line per transfer naming both
                              people and the amount; an empty list gives an empty array.

`balances` is {name: net} where net > 0 means that person is owed money.

You have NO TOOLS: no shell, no file access, no search. Everything you need is in this prompt. Output ONLY the file content - no markdown fence, no explanation, no leading or trailing prose.

Write frontend/index.html: one self-contained HTML page.

- It MUST contain elements with these exact ids: expense-form, balances, settlement.
- It MUST NOT reference any external URL - no CDN, no https:// and no // in any src or href.
  There is no network. Load only "./app.js" as a module.
- A form to add an expense (payer, amount, participants), and two empty containers for the
  balance summary and the settlement lines.

You have NO TOOLS: no shell, no file access, no search. Everything you need is in this prompt. Output ONLY the file content - no markdown fence, no explanation, no leading or trailing prose.

cmd:
import json, hashlib, pathlib
out = []
for f in ('backend/split.py', 'backend/server.py', 'frontend/split.js', 'frontend/index.html'):
    p = pathlib.Path(f)
    h = hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16] if p.is_file() else 'missing'
    out.append(f + '|' + h)
print(json.dumps({'schema_version': '1.0', 'files': out, 'notes': 'the four generated files'}))
